status: Frozen before inspecting holdout outcomes or fitting either model
question: How do retrospective predictive scores change when a documented post-call variable is added to a fixed profile/history model on the same later rows?
decisionPoint: Immediately before the recorded call. Profile and prior-campaign fields are assumed already available; the release has no feature-ingestion timestamps to validate this. Neither model is certified deployment-ready.

split.rule: Take the last complete contiguous month-label block ending at or before floor(0.70*N); preserve original file order. No shuffling or sorting by month/weekday.
split.dateLimit: Contiguous month-label blocks in publisher-declared chronological order; no year or full date is inferred. Rows are not verified unique clients.
split.validation: None: no tuning, threshold search or model selection. The holdout is evaluated once under this specification.

availabilityNotes.profile: Assume these profile fields were recorded before the call; timestamps are absent. Age and demographic attributes are descriptive inputs, not a recommendation to target groups.
availabilityNotes.history: Fields explicitly refer to prior campaigns. Assumed in the record before this call; no client identifiers or as-of feature store supplied.
availabilityNotes.excludedCallMetadata: Current/last-call communication, calendar and attempt-count fields are omitted to avoid needing a scheduled-call context assumption. Month is used only to define contiguous audit blocks.
availabilityNotes.excludedMacro: Publication lags and historical release vintages are not supplied; these fields are excluded from both models.
availabilityNotes.duration: Last-contact duration is known only after the call; included solely in the deliberately retrospective comparator.

preprocessing.pdays: pdays=999 maps to previouslyContacted=0 and pdaysObserved=0; otherwise previouslyContacted=1 and pdaysObserved=pdays. The indicator distinguishes never-contacted from zero observed days.
preprocessing.duration: Comparator adds log1p(duration_seconds), then training-only standardization. No other feature or transformation differs.
preprocessing.numericScaling: StandardScaler fitted on training rows only; population variance (ddof=0).
preprocessing.categoricalEncoding: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown=ignore,drop=None), categories learned only from training. Literal unknown remains a category if observed in training; unseen holdout levels map to all-zero indicators.
preprocessing.missing: Expected numeric fields must be finite; unexpected missing numeric values fail. No rows deleted and no label-dependent imputation.

model.convergence: Fail on ConvergenceWarning or n_iter reaching max_iter; do not change solver/hyperparameters after results.

metrics.averagePrecision: sklearn average_precision_score: noninterpolated average precision, not trapezoidal PR-AUC. Null when there are no positives.
metrics.brier: Mean squared error of uncalibrated logistic probability and binary outcome; smaller is better.
metrics.baseline: Constant probability equal to training prevalence; no holdout fitting or recalibration. Its average precision equals holdout prevalence.
metrics.budgetRule: Select ceil(0.10*N) largest scores within the complete retrospective evaluation batch; break exact score ties by source row ordinal ascending. This is not a prospective online call-allocation policy.
metrics.calibrationRule: Fixed equal-width bins; left-closed/right-open except final includes1. Empty bins retained with null means/rates. No recalibration.

resampling.method: Paired resampling with replacement of the 18 complete heldout contiguous month-label blocks; fit models once and retain predictions; use exactly the same drawn block indices for both models.
resampling.differences: withDuration minus withoutDuration for averagePrecision, brier and precisionAtBudget; negative Brier difference favors duration.
resampling.undefined: Count undefined/no-positive AP replicates explicitly and exclude them from that metric interval only; do not substitute zero.
resampling.interpretation: Descriptive block-resampling sensitivity ranges, not iid confidence intervals, population uncertainty, or a guarantee about future campaigns. Blocks and repeated clients can remain dependent. Replicate row counts vary with block sizes.

recordBrowser.coverage: All heldout rows; anonymous original row ordinal only, no invented identity.
recordBrowser.defaultRule: Largest absolute difference between the two predicted probabilities; ties by source row ordinal. Labels do not select showcased records.

limits: Known timing hazard documented by the source, not a newly discovered theory.
Observational campaign outcomes do not identify effects of calling, targeting, budget changes or call duration.
Chronological records are not verified client-disjoint; no client identifiers or full timestamps are supplied.
The source may record last campaign contacts; its rows are not a fully specified online decision log.
Results concern one institution and historical release; no representative generalization or prospective deployment claim.
